scope: FDIC deposit-insurance rules and the official national rate benchmarks used throughout this project.

coverage_limits.rule: All single accounts owned by the same person at the same bank are added together and insured up to $250,000.
Each co-owner's shares of every joint account at the same insured bank are added together and insured up to $250,000 per co-owner.
All retirement accounts listed by the FDIC owned by the same person at the same bank are added together and insured up to $250,000.
FDIC formula: # of owners x # of beneficiaries x $250,000, not to exceed $1,250,000 per owner for all trust accounts.
Each participant's non-contingent interest is insured up to $250,000 per bank; for contingent interests (e.g., health and welfare plans) coverage is $250,000 for the plan itself.

covered_products: Prepaid cards (assuming certain FDIC requirements are met)
not_covered_products: Safe deposit boxes or their contents
U.S. Treasury bills, bonds or notes

key_rules.text: FDIC insurance is automatic for deposit accounts at an FDIC-insured bank; depositors do not apply for it.
Coverage is at least $250,000 per depositor, per ownership category, at each FDIC-insured bank.
All deposits in the same ownership category at the same bank are added together when coverage is calculated.
A single-ownership savings account at one bank is therefore capped at $250,000 of FDIC insurance; amounts above that at the same bank in the same category are uninsured.

national_rates.publication: FDIC National Rates and Rate Caps - October 2026 (revised rule October 19, 2026)

treasury_yields_pct.note: Treasury yields published in the same FDIC table; used here only as a benchmark, not as an FDIC-insured product.

rate_cap_note.text: The FDIC national rate cap applies to less-than-well-capitalized institutions and is not a market rate for consumers. For savings it is 4.63% as of 2026-10-19.
